title: Skull base and temporal bone

steps.tx: Paragangliomas of the posterior skull base exhibit aggressive bony remodelling. A **Glomus jugulare** paraganglioma causes permeative moth-eaten bone destruction centered on the **jugular foramen**, displaying a characteristic salt-and-pepper pattern on magnetic resonance imaging from subacute haemorrhage and high-velocity flow voids.

steps.tx: Acquired middle ear keratomas present with persistent purulent otorrhea and progressive ossicular erosion. An acquired **cholesteatoma** originates classically within the epitympanic **Prussak space**, blunts the adjacent bony scutum, and exhibits pathognomonic restricted diffusion on non-echo planar diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance sequences.

vis.alt: Axial CT shows scutum erosion and air in the lateral semicircular canal, indicating cholesteatoma and labyrinthine fistula.
vis.caption: Cholesteatoma: scutum erosion, pneumolabyrinth (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Otic capsule dysplasias manifest with conductive or mixed auditory decline. Fenestral **otosclerosis** features focal bone demineralisation and radiolucency immediately anterior to the oval window at the **fissula ante fenestram** on high-resolution temporal bone computed tomography, leading to progressive stapedial footplate fixation.

steps.tx: Asymmetric auditory decline demands targeted neuroimaging of the cerebellopontine angle. Significant **sensorineural hearing loss** of retrocochlear etiology most frequently results from a benign **vestibular schwannoma**, which causes trumpet-like flaring of the porus acusticus, widening of the internal auditory canal, and intense contrast enhancement on magnetic resonance imaging.

vis.alt: Axial contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrating an ice-cream cone shaped vestibular schwannoma within the cerebellopontine angle.
vis.caption: Vestibular schwannoma: cerebellopontine angle mass with internal auditory canal expansion (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Midline cranial base neoplasms present unique imaging characteristics reflecting their primitive embryological origins. A skull base **chordoma** arises from embryonic notochord remnants, classically centered within the midline **clivus**, displaying profound T2 hyperintensity, destructive bone lysis, and lobulated honeycomb contrast enhancement.

steps.tx: Cartilaginous neoplasms of the skull base arise laterally compared to midline chordomas. A skull base **chondrosarcoma** originates off-midline along the **petroclival synchondrosis**, characteristically displaying rings-and-arcs chondroid matrix calcifications on computed tomography and bright lobulated T2 hyperintensity on magnetic resonance imaging.

steps.tx: Extension of acute middle ear inflammation into pneumatic cell tracts leads to severe cranial nerve morbidity. Unchecked **petrous apicitis** generates **Gradenigo syndrome**, presenting the classic clinical triad of retro-orbital pain, ipsilateral abducens nerve palsy, and continuous purulent otorrhea from adjacent suppurative mastoiditis.

steps.tx: Cutaneous and salivary malignancies frequently spread along neural highways without primary mass enlargement. High-resolution magnetic resonance imaging detects **perineural tumour spread** along the fifth and seventh **cranial nerves**, recognised by abnormal nerve thickening, intense perineural enhancement, and obliteration of normal neural foramen fat pads.
